shots.title: Net worth, households 65–74
shots.src: Nest Egg Atlas calculation from the Federal Reserve's 2025 Survey of Consumer Finances public data (survey weights) · households by age of head · 2025 dollars

bars.label: Top 25% from
bars.at: To be in the top quarter

bars.label: Top 10% from
bars.at: to be in the top ten percent

shots.narration: The Federal Reserve recently released its newest survey of American family finances, and it answers a question a lot of people quietly wonder about: how do I compare? {p} For households where the head is sixty-five to seventy-four, here's the ladder. {p} The bottom quarter has less than about a hundred and eighteen thousand dollars in net worth. {p} The typical household, right in the middle, has about four hundred and thirty-one thousand. {p} To be in the top quarter, you need about one point three million. {p} And to be in the top ten percent, about three point six million dollars. {pp} So the top ten percent starts at more than eight times what the typical household has.

In this video, we'll look at what actually counts in that number, the full ladder from the bottom to the very top, how many retirees are millionaires and what their money is made of, how it changes with age, and the part of the picture that's easy to miss: the households at the bottom. {p} These are real survey numbers, not estimates from a calculator: about twenty-two million households in this age group, measured by the Federal Reserve. {pp} <soft>As always, this is education, not financial advice.</soft>

shots.title: What counts in net worth
shots.src: Federal Reserve, Survey of Consumer Finances: net worth = assets minus debts (excludes Social Security and defined-benefit pensions)
shots.narration: First, what goes into that number. {p} Net worth is everything a household owns, minus everything it owes. {p} That includes the home: what it's worth, minus the mortgage. {p} Retirement accounts like 401(k)s and IRAs. {p} Savings, stocks, bonds, and any business. {p} Cars count too. Minus every debt: the mortgage, car loans, credit cards. {pp} And one thing is left out: the value of future Social Security checks and traditional pensions. For many retirees, those are worth a lot, and they don't show up here at all.

The home is a big part of it. About eighty percent of households in this age group own their home, and the median household has about two hundred and ten thousand dollars of home equity. {p} Take the home out, and the typical net worth drops from about four hundred and thirty-one thousand to about a hundred and forty thousand. {pp} In the middle of the ladder, the house does a lot of the work. Near the top, as we'll see, it's a much smaller share. {p} And for renters, there's no home equity at all, which is one reason the bottom of the ladder looks so different.

shots.title: The full ladder, ages 65–74
shots.sub: Net worth where each group starts · 2025
shots.src: Nest Egg Atlas calculation from the Federal Reserve's 2025 Survey of Consumer Finances public data (survey weights) · households by age of head · 2025 dollars
shots.narration: Here's the whole ladder. {p} The bottom ten percent: less than about sixty-five hundred dollars. {p} The bottom quarter: less than about a hundred and eighteen thousand. {p} The middle: about four hundred and thirty-one thousand. {p} The top quarter starts at about one point three million. {p} The top ten percent, at about three point six million. {p} And the top five percent, at about seven point one million. {pp} The very top one percent starts at about twenty and a half million dollars. {p} Between the start of the top five percent and the bottom ten percent, that's a difference of more than a thousand times.

Notice how fast it climbs at the top. Going from the middle to the start of the top quarter means about three times more. From there to the top ten percent, almost three times again. {p} That's also why the average is so misleading. The average net worth for this age group is about one point nine million dollars. That's more than four times the median, because a relatively small number of very wealthy households pull it up. {pp} When you see an average in a headline, the typical household is usually far below it. Medians are the fairer way to compare.

shots.title: Households 65–74 with at least…
shots.src: Nest Egg Atlas calculation from the Federal Reserve's 2025 Survey of Consumer Finances public data (survey weights) · households by age of head · 2025 dollars
shots.narration: So how many retirees are millionaires? More than you might think. {p} About forty-five percent of households aged sixty-five to seventy-four have at least half a million dollars. {p} About thirty-one percent have at least a million. {p} About nineteen percent, at least two million. {p} And about eight percent, at least five million. {pp} That's roughly one in three households in this age group with a seven-figure net worth: about six point eight million households.

So what does a typical millionaire household at this age look like? {p} Its median net worth is about two and a half million dollars. Almost all of them, ninety-eight percent, own their home, with about five hundred and seventy-five thousand dollars of equity. {p} The typical one has about six hundred and sixty thousand dollars in retirement accounts, and an income of about a hundred and forty thousand a year. {pp} But the home is usually only about a fifth of their net worth. Much more of their money is in financial assets: the typical one has about one point three million dollars in stocks, funds, savings and retirement accounts combined. {p} In other words, most millionaire retirees didn't get there through their house alone.

shots.title: Median net worth by age
shots.src: Nest Egg Atlas calculation from the Federal Reserve's 2025 Survey of Consumer Finances public data (survey weights) · households by age of head · 2025 dollars
shots.narration: Here's something that surprises people: in this survey, net worth doesn't fall after retirement. It keeps rising. {p} The typical household aged fifty-five to sixty-four has about four hundred and eleven thousand. {p} Sixty-five to seventy-four: about four hundred and thirty-one thousand. {p} Seventy-five and older: about five hundred and four thousand. {pp} The top ten percent line rises too: from about three point five million, to about three point six, to about four point two million for households seventy-five and older.

Part of that is the home. Older households have usually paid down more of their mortgage, and home values have risen. The median household's home equity goes from about a hundred and fifty-eight thousand at fifty-five to sixty-four, to about two hundred and forty-five thousand at seventy-five and older. {p} Part of it is who's in the group. People with more money tend to live longer, so the oldest group is a bit wealthier on average. {pp} And this is a snapshot of different generations in 2025, not one family followed over time. So compare yourself with your own age group, not with a single national number.

items.at: Part of that is the home

shots.title: The other end of the ladder, ages 65–74
shots.src: Nest Egg Atlas calculation from the Federal Reserve's 2025 Survey of Consumer Finances public data (survey weights) · households by age of head · 2025 dollars

stats.at: a net worth of zero or less
stats.label: zero or negative net worth

shots.narration: Now the other end. {p} About five percent of households in this age group have a net worth of zero or less: they owe as much as they own, or more. {p} The bottom ten percent has less than about sixty-five hundred dollars. {p} And the typical household has about ten thousand dollars in checking and savings accounts. {pp} For many of the households near the bottom, Social Security isn't one part of retirement income. It's most of it. That's why the size of that monthly check matters so much.

And what about income? For households aged sixty-five to seventy-four, the median income in this survey is about seventy thousand dollars a year. To be in the top ten percent by income, it takes about two hundred and thirty-five thousand. {p} The bottom ten percent by income have about twenty thousand dollars a year or less. {p} Income and wealth don't always line up. Plenty of retirees have a modest income and a paid-off house worth a lot. And some have a high income and very little saved. {pp} Both numbers matter. Net worth is how long your money can last. Income is how comfortable each year feels.

shots.title: Where do you stand? Ages 65–74
shots.src: Nest Egg Atlas calculation from the Federal Reserve's 2025 Survey of Consumer Finances public data (survey weights) · households by age of head · 2025 dollars
shots.narration: So here's where the lines fall for households aged sixty-five to seventy-four. {p} Under about a hundred and eighteen thousand puts you in the bottom quarter. {p} Around four hundred and thirty thousand is the middle. {p} About one point three million puts you in the top quarter. {p} About three point six million, in the top ten percent. {p} And about twenty and a half million, in the top one percent. {pp} And remember: these numbers leave out Social Security and traditional pensions, which for many people are worth hundreds of thousands of dollars more. {p} And for households seventy-five and older, every line is a little higher: the middle is about five hundred thousand, and the top ten percent starts at about four point two million.

items.at: Under about a hundred and eighteen
puts you in the top quarter

shots.narration: Tell me in the comments: were you surprised by where the median is? {p} And if you know someone who's sure they're behind, send them this. They might be doing better than they think.
Net worth is the big picture. If you want to see what's actually in the typical retirement account, watch this next. {p} This is Nest Egg Atlas. See you next time.

Take your time with every dollar figure and let it land with a short pause before it. Read only the script, word for word. Sound reassuring and clear, never rushed, never salesy, never alarmed, never like an advertisement.

yt.title: What Net Worth Puts You in the Top 10% at 65–74? (New Fed Data)
yt.description:
How does your net worth compare with other households aged 65 to 74? Using the Federal Reserve's 2025 Survey of Consumer Finances, we calculate the full ladder (bottom 10%, bottom 25%, median, top 25%, top 10%, top 5%, top 1%), what counts in net worth, how many retirees are millionaires and what their money is made of, how net worth changes from 55 to 75+, and the households at the bottom.

Net worth = assets minus debts, including home equity and retirement accounts; it does not include Social Security or traditional pensions.

Educational content, not financial advice.

Sources: Federal Reserve Board, 2025 Survey of Consumer Finances, summary extract public data (our calculation with survey weights; 2025 dollars).
{music_credits}
Narration is AI-generated.
